description: Auto-mark an epic done when all its linked issues complete, reusing the existing readiness check; paused epics are excluded and resume re-evaluates.

tasks.title: Epic auto-done grain capability + resume re-evaluation
tasks.description: Add an idempotent `AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync` method to IEpicGrain/EpicGrain that, when the epic is `active` and all linked issues are complete (undelivered count == 0, reusing ComputeUndeliveredLinkedNumbersAsync + domain.MarkDone), transitions to `done`; when terminal (`done`/`closed`) or `paused` it is a no-op returning the current DTO without throwing. Also wire EpicGrain.ResumeAsync to re-evaluate readiness in-turn after a successful paused→active transition, so a ready epic auto-dones on resume without waiting for a fresh issue event.
acceptanceCriteria: AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync transitions an active epic with all linked issues done/completed to `done`.
Calling AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync on an already-terminal (done/closed) or paused epic is a no-op and throws nothing (idempotent).
AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync with at least one incomplete linked issue leaves the epic `active`.
Cancelled linked issues are not treated as complete (matches manual MarkDone) — epic stays active.
ResumeAsync on a paused epic whose linked issues are all complete transitions through active and ends in `done`; resume with incomplete issues ends in `active`.
Fake-based unit tests cover all above cases (no real DB/OS/external systems); server build (dotnet build) succeeds with warnings-as-errors.
Manual SetStatusAsync("done") behavior and its errors are unchanged (regression check).
tasks.output: IEpicGrain.AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync + ResumeAsync re-evaluation + unit tests in packages/server
tasks.notes: Do NOT change the readiness definition or Epic.MarkDone throw semantics; only the new auto method swallows terminal/paused. Reuse ComputeUndeliveredLinkedNumbersAsync.

tasks.title: Issue-completion event → epic auto-done wiring
tasks.description: Wire event-driven auto-done: add a reverse `GetEpicIdForIssueAsync(projectId, issueId)` lookup in EpicQuerier (uses existing IX_EpicIssues_ProjectId_IssueId index), and a new [Subscription(Type = "com.mohist.issue.work-completed")] CloudEvent handler that resolves the owning epic and invokes IEpicGrain.AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync. When the issue is not linked to any epic, the handler no-ops. The handler must tolerate duplicate/out-of-order events by relying on the grain's idempotency.
acceptanceCriteria: When the last linked issue of an active epic completes (com.mohist.issue.work-completed), the epic auto-transitions to `done` with no manual action.
When a completing issue is linked to no epic, the handler no-ops without error.
When a completing issue's epic still has incomplete linked issues, the epic stays `active`.
Duplicate or out-of-order work-completed events for the same epic converge to the correct state with no errors (relies on T-001 idempotency).
Fake-based tests cover: last-issue-completes→done, unlinked issue no-op, partial completion no-op, duplicate event idempotent, paused epic unchanged on event (no auto-done).
dotnet build succeeds with warnings-as-errors; handler is auto-discovered via AddCloudEventHandlersFromAssembly (no manual registration).
tasks.output: EpicQuerier.GetEpicIdForIssueAsync + EpicAutoDoneHandler [Subscription] + unit tests in packages/server
tasks.notes: Event extensions projectid/issueid/issueno are already published (IssueGrain.cs:529). Do not introduce Orleans streams. Handler runs post-commit (issue persisted before publish).

tasks.title: Epic readiness reconciliation safety-net
tasks.description: Add a self-healing sweep that compensates for the in-memory CloudEvent bus being at-most-once / swallow-on-failure (PublishIssueEventsAsync try/catch→log). It identifies epics whose EpicProgress reports ReadyToMarkDone but whose status is still `active`, and invokes AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync on each, so a missed completion event does not leave a ready epic stuck. Pick the cheapest existing periodic/triggered surface to host the sweep (e.g. alongside issue-workflow reconciliation).
acceptanceCriteria: A ready-but-active epic (ReadyToMarkDone == true, status == active) is transitioned to `done` by the sweep.
Paused and terminal epics are skipped by the sweep (paused exclusion preserved).
Sweep is idempotent and safe to run repeatedly (re-entrancy handled by AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync).
Fake-based tests cover: missed-event recovery, paused skip, idempotent re-run.
dotnet build succeeds with warnings-as-errors; no DB schema or config change.
tasks.output: Epic readiness reconciliation sweep + unit tests in packages/server
tasks.notes: Cadence host is the open question from design.md — reuse an existing periodic surface rather than introducing a new timer infra. If no suitable surface exists, fall back to a simple reminder-backed tick and document the choice.
